'''''Scabiosa columbaria''''', called the '''small scabious''' or '''dwarf pincushion flower''', is a widespread species of flowering plant in the genus ''[[Scabiosa]]'', native to Europe, Africa, and western Asia, from Sweden to Angola.<ref name="319793-1" >{{cite web |url=http://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:319793-1 |title=''Scabiosa columbaria'' L. |author=<!--Not stated--> |date=2017 |website=Plants of the World Online |publisher=Board of Trustees of the Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew |access-date=31 December 2020 }}</ref><ref name = RHSPF>{{cite web |title=''Scabiosa columbaria'' small scabious |url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/16772/Scabiosa-columbaria/Details |publisher=The Royal Horticultural Society |access-date=31 December 2020 |quote=Other common names; lilac-flowered scabious }}</ref> In the garden it is a short-lived [[deciduous]] [[perennial plant|perennial]].<ref>{{cite book |title=When Perennials Bloom: An Almanac for Planning and Planting |last1=Ani Ko |first1=Tomasz |page=413 |date=January 2008 |isbn=9780881928877 }}</ref> In the wild in Europe it prefers to grow in [[calcareous]] [[grassland]]s.<ref name="1_of_5560_Google_Scholar_Hits" >{{cite journal |title=Land use affects flowering time: Seasonal and genetic differentiation in the grassland plant ''Scabiosa columbaria'' |year=2009 |last1=Reisch |first1=Christoph |last2=Poschlod |first2=Peter |journal=Evolutionary Ecology |volume=23 |issue=5 |pages=753–764 |doi=10.1007/s10682-008-9270-4 |bibcode=2009EvEco..23..753R |s2cid=32021366 }}</ref>

Growing to {{convert|1|m|ft|abbr=on}} tall by {{convert|0.5|m|ft|abbr=on}}, it has simple branched grey-green leaves, and pale lavender or blue multi-petalled flowers from summer to autumn.<ref name = RHSPF/>

*''Scabiosa columbaria'' subsp. ''columbaria''
*''Scabiosa columbaria'' subsp. ''pratensis'' <small>(St.-Lag.) Braun-Blanq.</small>
